key_insight: KVEraser learns how to selectively steer the KV cache so a local span can be erased without needing to fully recompute the entire later context. This makes post-hoc context removal practical for long-context LLMs.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the difficulty of exact context erasing in KV caches, where deleting a span normally forces recomputation of all subsequent tokens because earlier information has already propagated through cached states.
method: Learns a steering mechanism over the KV cache to localize the effect of erasure.
Targets only the necessary cache updates instead of reprocessing the full post-edit sequence.
Aims to preserve model behavior while removing stale, incorrect, or harmful context after prefill.
impact: This helps AI practitioners handle long-context applications more efficiently when they need to remove bad information after it has already been processed. It can reduce compute cost and latency for safer, more controllable LLM systems.
visual_elements: A before/after KV cache flow diagram showing full recomputation vs. localized erasure.
An attention or token timeline highlighting the deleted span and affected future tokens.
A cache block graphic illustrating which states are updated versus preserved.
Icons for stale facts, tool errors, user preference changes, and prompt injection to show use cases.
paper_title: KVEraser: Learning to Steer KV Cache for Efficient Localized Context Erasing
paper_authors: Mufei Li, Shikun Liu, Dongqi Fu, Haoyu Wang, Yinglong Xia
